cultural.vision_reason: This is a Sámi shaman's frame drum (goavddis) with reindeer-skin membrane bearing faint painted/incised ritual figures, a well-documented traditional Sámi instrument used in noaidi ceremonies.

physical.title: drum; religious/ritual equipment
physical.summary:
Drum, made of wood and skin, of frame drum type, with painted designs and figures on membrane for use in magic ceremonies. The reindeer skin membrane bound at the edge and sewn onto the wood frame with a thread made of skin. Some of the motifs on the membrane are inscised as well as coloured, especially those round the outer edge. The frame formed of a single curved piece of wood, which overlaps at one side and is bound with white metal lozenge-shaped rivets, a leather thong, and a brass strip with copper rivets. At top of frame is a rectangular recess, echoed by a rectangular hole of the same size at the bottom of the frame, to take bar of wood as a handle (lacking). The exterior of the frame decorated with incised lines. At the bask, at the wider end hang amulets in the form of leather cords, threaded through the frame; these divide into three cords formed of twisted leather strips and bound with metal wire.  
     A nineteenth century circular label on the frame reads: 'Pres'd by A.W. Franks 1 1869. Klemm Coll.'
